sdcards.name: SanDisk Extreme microSD
sdcards.pros: V30 and A2 with fast writes, sold up to 1.5TB. Widely available, so easy to buy genuine.
sdcards.cons: Write speeds are lower on the 32GB and 64GB versions.

sdcards.name: SanDisk Extreme microSD (Action Cam Edition)
sdcards.pros: Highest sustained read/write speeds in the Extreme microSD line. Built for 4K/5.3K action cam footage.
sdcards.cons: No A2 app performance rating. Tuned for sustained video, not app storage.
sdcards.notes: Distinct higher-speed SKU from the standard SanDisk Extreme microSD (this one foregoes A2 rating for faster sequential speeds); sold separately and marketed specifically for action cameras.

sdcards.name: Samsung EVO Select (Blue)
sdcards.pros: Low price per GB with V30 and A2. 10-year limited warranty.
sdcards.cons: Writes slower than the SanDisk Extreme.

sdcards.name: Lexar Professional 633x (Blue Series)
sdcards.pros: Budget V30 card for 1080p and 4K up to 100 Mbps.
sdcards.cons: Much slower than Lexar Silver and Gold.

sdcards.name: Kingston Canvas Go! Plus
sdcards.pros: V30 and A2 with 90 MB/s writes. Often bundled with a USB reader.
sdcards.cons: Less common in retail stores than SanDisk.

sdcards.name: Kingston Canvas Go! Plus (Mapped)
sdcards.pros: V30 and A2 with 90 MB/s writes. Often bundled with a USB reader.
sdcards.cons: Less common in retail stores than SanDisk.

sdcards.name: Kingston Canvas Go! (Legacy)
sdcards.pros: Older V30 card, fine if found cheap.
sdcards.cons: Replaced by the faster Canvas Go! Plus.

sdcards.name: Lexar Professional Gold (1800x)
sdcards.pros: UHS-II microSD that reads up to 280 MB/s in a UHS-II reader.
sdcards.cons: Costs more per GB. Runs at UHS-I speed in drones, action cams and other UHS-I slots.

sdcards.name: Lexar Professional Silver (1066x)
sdcards.pros: V30 card with 120 MB/s writes at a mid-range price.
sdcards.cons: Needs a Lexar reader for the full 160 MB/s read speed.

sdcards.name: SanDisk Ultra microSD
sdcards.pros: Cheap and sold in large capacities up to 1.5TB.
sdcards.cons: Not V30 rated. Too slow for most 4K video.

sdcards.name: Kingston Canvas Select Plus
sdcards.pros: Low price with a lifetime limited warranty.
sdcards.cons: Not V30 rated. Avoid for 4K.

sdcards.name: SanDisk MAX ENDURANCE
sdcards.pros: Rated for up to 120,000 hours of recording (256GB). Built for 24/7 dash cams and security cameras.
sdcards.cons: Slower writes than standard cards of the same price.

sdcards.name: SanDisk High Endurance microSD
sdcards.pros: Rated for continuous dash cam and security camera recording, sold up to 512GB.
sdcards.cons: Lower endurance rating than the MAX Endurance line.

sdcards.name: Samsung PRO Endurance
sdcards.pros: Rated for up to 140,000 hours of recording (256GB). A common pick for dash cams.
sdcards.cons: Built for endurance, not speed.

sdcards.name: Lexar Play microSD
sdcards.pros: Low price per GB in 1TB. A2 rated for game loading on Switch and handhelds.
sdcards.cons: Writes slower than Lexar Silver. Sold for gaming rather than cameras.

sdcards.name: SanDisk microSD for ROG Ally
sdcards.pros: ASUS-licensed version of the SanDisk Extreme, in 512GB and 1TB.
sdcards.cons: Costs more than the standard Extreme with the same specs.

sdcards.name: ADATA Premier microSD
sdcards.pros: Very cheap.
sdcards.cons: Slow writes. Not for 4K video.

sdcards.name: Transcend 300S microSD
sdcards.pros: Budget V30 card.
sdcards.cons: Slower random reads than A2 cards.

sdcards.name: ADATA Premier Pro microSD
sdcards.pros: V30 and A2 at a low price.
sdcards.cons: Harder to find than SanDisk and Samsung.

sdcards.name: SanDisk Extreme PRO microSD UHS-II
sdcards.pros: UHS-II microSD that reads up to 280 MB/s in a UHS-II reader.
sdcards.cons: Expensive. Runs at UHS-I speed in drones and other UHS-I slots.

sdcards.name: SanDisk Extreme PRO microSD UHS-I (2TB)
sdcards.pros: Sold up to 2TB, the microSDXC maximum. V30 and A2 for gaming handhelds and cameras.
sdcards.cons: Expensive at the top capacities.

sdcards.name: SanDisk Extreme PRO CFexpress Type B
sdcards.pros: A common choice for the Canon R5 and Nikon Z8 and Z9.
sdcards.cons: Runs warm during long 8K recording.

sdcards.name: Lexar Professional Gold (1800x) V60
sdcards.pros: V60 UHS-II card with 205 MB/s writes at a lower price than most V90 cards.
sdcards.cons: Needs a UHS-II slot to use its speed.

sdcards.name: SanDisk Extreme PRO SD UHS-II
sdcards.pros: V90 UHS-II card for high-bitrate video and fast bursts.
sdcards.cons: High cost per GB.

sdcards.name: Lexar Professional Silver SD
sdcards.pros: V30 SD card with 120 MB/s writes at a mid-range price.
sdcards.cons: Write speed drops once its cache fills during long bursts.

sdcards.name: Kingston Canvas Go! Plus SD (Mapped)
sdcards.pros: Fast UHS-I SD card with 90 MB/s writes.
sdcards.cons: Easy to confuse with Kingston's Canvas React line.

sdcards.name: Gigastone 128GB SD Card 4K Camera Pro
sdcards.pros: 100MB/s read speed. A1 app performance for shooting RAW+JPEG. Includes mini case. 5-year data recovery service.
sdcards.cons: UHS-I only, not suited to high-bitrate 4K/6K cinema cameras needing V60/V90. Only sold in 128GB. Amazon's listing title advertises 150MB/s but the card packaging itself is printed 100MB/s - we use the packaging figure.
sdcards.notes: Sponsored - Creator Connections product (tag=uproot01-20). Speed listed as printed on packaging (100MB/s), not the 150MB/s figure in Amazon's listing title - verify against current listing before reusing this claim elsewhere.

sdcards.name: Nikon XQD Memory Card
sdcards.pros: Nikon-branded XQD card for the D850, D500, Z6 and Z7.
sdcards.cons: XQD is a legacy format. CFexpress Type B fits the same slots on most of these cameras after a firmware update.

sdcards.name: SanDisk Extreme PRO CFast 2.0
sdcards.pros: VPG-130 rated for cinema cameras such as Blackmagic and Canon C-series.
sdcards.cons: High price per GB.

sdcards.name: Sony TOUGH G-Series SD
sdcards.pros: One-piece molded body rated for drops, water and bending. Writes up to 299 MB/s.
sdcards.cons: Expensive.

sdcards.name: Kingston Canvas React Plus SD
sdcards.pros: V90 UHS-II card at a lower price than Sony and SanDisk V90 cards.
sdcards.cons: Harder to find in stores.

sdcards.name: SanDisk Extreme PRO CFexpress Type A
sdcards.pros: Handles every recording mode on Sony bodies with Type A slots, including 4K120 All-Intra.
sdcards.cons: Expensive per GB.

sdcards.name: Lexar Professional 1667x Silver SD (Legacy ID)
sdcards.pros: Low-cost way into UHS-II SD.
sdcards.cons: V60, not V90. Too slow for All-Intra 4K.

sdcards.name: SanDisk Extreme SD UHS-I
sdcards.pros: V30 SD card that covers most 4K cameras.
sdcards.cons: Clears the buffer slower than UHS-II cards.

sdcards.name: SanDisk Ultra SD UHS-I
sdcards.pros: Cheap and reliable for photos and 1080p.
sdcards.cons: Not V30 rated. Not for 4K video.

sdcards.name: Lexar Professional 633x SD (Blue Series)
sdcards.pros: Budget V30 SD card.
sdcards.cons: Slower than Lexar Silver and Gold.

sdcards.name: SanDisk Extreme PRO SD UHS-I
sdcards.pros: Among the fastest UHS-I SD cards, with V30 and fast buffer clearing.
sdcards.cons: Costs more than the SanDisk Extreme.
sdcards.notes: Specs reflect the current-generation SDSDXXJ SKU (250 MB/s read / 120 MB/s write). An earlier SDSDXXD revision trades a slightly lower read speed for a higher 140 MB/s write, so check the exact SKU if write speed matters more than read speed for your use case.

sdcards.name: Kingston High Endurance microSD
sdcards.pros: Budget endurance card for light security camera use.
sdcards.cons: Lower endurance rating than Samsung PRO Endurance and SanDisk MAX Endurance.

sdcards.name: Amazon Basics Micro SDXC
sdcards.pros: Low price with A2 for apps and U3 for 4K up to about 100 Mbps.
sdcards.cons: Slower sustained writes than premium cards.

sdcards.name: Samsung PRO Plus microSD
sdcards.pros: V30 and A2 with 120 MB/s writes for 4K video and apps.
sdcards.cons: Costs more than the Samsung EVO Select.

sdcards.name: Kingston Canvas React Plus microSD
sdcards.pros: UHS-II microSD that reads up to 320 MB/s in a UHS-II reader or slot.
sdcards.cons: High cost per GB. Runs at UHS-I speed in UHS-I devices.

sdcards.name: SanDisk Nintendo Switch: Legend of Zelda Tears of the Kingdom
sdcards.pros: Nintendo-licensed design. Same speed as SanDisk's other Switch cards, up to 1TB.
sdcards.cons: Costs more than unbranded cards with the same speed.
sdcards.notes: UHS-I only. Works in all Nintendo Switch models but will not utilize SD Express speeds in Nintendo Switch 2.

sdcards.name: SanDisk Nintendo Switch: Pokémon Gengar
sdcards.pros: Gengar design, 512GB.
sdcards.cons: Only sold in 512GB.
sdcards.notes: UHS-I only. Backward compatible with Switch 2 but limited by UHS-I speed ceiling.

sdcards.name: SanDisk Nintendo Switch: Pokémon Snorlax
sdcards.pros: 1TB holds a large Switch library.
sdcards.cons: Costs more than unbranded 1TB cards.
sdcards.notes: UHS-I only. Perfect for digital-focused Switch owners.

sdcards.name: SanDisk Nintendo Switch: Pokémon Pikachu
sdcards.pros: Pikachu design, 256GB.
sdcards.cons: Only sold in 256GB.
sdcards.notes: UHS-I only. Great for collectors and casual gamers.

sdcards.name: SanDisk Nintendo Switch: Yoshi Edition
sdcards.pros: Yoshi design in 64GB and 128GB.
sdcards.cons: 64GB and 128GB fill quickly with recent games.
sdcards.notes: UHS-I only. Best for indie game collections.

sdcards.name: SanDisk Nintendo Switch: Animal Crossing Leaf
sdcards.pros: Animal Crossing design in 256GB and 512GB.
sdcards.cons: Costs more for the licensed design.
sdcards.notes: UHS-I only. Themed for relaxed players.

sdcards.name: SanDisk Nintendo Switch: Super Mario Mushroom
sdcards.pros: Super Mushroom design in 64GB to 256GB.
sdcards.cons: Costs more for the licensed design.
sdcards.notes: UHS-I only. Perfect for Super Mario enthusiasts.

sdcards.name: SanDisk Nintendo Switch: Super Mario Super Star
sdcards.pros: Super Star design in 128GB and 256GB.
sdcards.cons: Higher cost per GB than unbranded cards.
sdcards.notes: UHS-I only. Great for Mario franchise fans.

sdcards.name: SanDisk Nintendo Switch: Fortnite Cuddle Team Leader
sdcards.pros: Fortnite Cuddle Team Leader design, 128GB.
sdcards.cons: Only sold in 128GB.
sdcards.notes: UHS-I only. Ideal for Fortnite players on Switch.

sdcards.name: SanDisk Nintendo Switch: Fortnite Skull Trooper
sdcards.pros: Fortnite Skull Trooper design, 256GB.
sdcards.cons: Costs more for the licensed design.
sdcards.notes: UHS-I only. Limited to UHS-I speeds.

sdcards.name: Topesel High Endurance (2-Pack)
sdcards.pros: Two-pack sold as high endurance for dash cams.
sdcards.cons: No published endurance rating in hours. Write speed varies by capacity.
sdcards.notes: 20% Commission. Specifically designed for high-write applications like dash cams.

sdcards.name: Speederlash Class 10 (2-Pack)
sdcards.pros: Cheap two-pack of Class 10 cards for basic dash cams.
sdcards.cons: No endurance rating. Not for 24/7 recording.
sdcards.notes: 10% Commission. Good entry-level option for casual dash cam users.

sdcards.name: Navtimi 2025 Toyota Navigation SD Card
sdcards.pros: Covers 10 Toyota models. Plug and play. 2025 maps included.
sdcards.cons: Toyota-specific only. Confirm factory nav is installed.

sdcards.name: 2025 Toyota Navigation SD Card (Part 86271-0E077)
sdcards.pros: Exact OEM part number match. Budget-friendly alternative to Navtimi.
sdcards.cons: Fewer compatible models than Navtimi.

sdcards.name: ORIRI·X 2025 Navigation SD Card for GM (Part 85856394)
sdcards.pros: 2025 maps. Fits Chevrolet, Cadillac, Buick, GMC. Plug and play.
sdcards.cons: Verify part number 85856394 matches your existing card.

sdcards.name: Premium 2025 GM Navigation SD Card (Part 85713512, 10yr Warranty)
sdcards.pros: 10-year warranty. 2025 maps. Premium tier.
sdcards.cons: Higher price. Verify part 85713512 matches your card.

sdcards.name: 2024 GPS Navigation SD Card for GM (Part 85713512)
sdcards.pros: Cheapest option for Part 85713512 vehicles.
sdcards.cons: 2024 maps, not 2025.

sdcards.name: DIGIERA 64GB CT100 microSDXC
sdcards.pros: 100 MB/s read. A1 rated. Comes with adapter. Very affordable.
sdcards.cons: V10 speed only, not suitable for 4K video recording.

sdcards.name: Speederlash 64GB 2-Pack Camera Plus
sdcards.pros: 2-pack value. V30 + A1. Includes adapter. Good for security cameras and dash cams.
sdcards.cons: 64GB only. Generic brand.

sdcards.name: ProGrade Digital CFexpress Type B Gold
sdcards.pros: Common choice for Nikon Z8 and Z9 and Canon R5 8K. High sustained writes keep the buffer clear.
sdcards.cons: Costs more than most shooters need for 4K.

sdcards.name: Angelbird AV PRO CFexpress Type B MK2
sdcards.pros: Holds its write speed through long cinema takes on the Z8, Z9 and similar bodies.
sdcards.cons: No capacities under 1TB.

sdcards.name: Sony TOUGH CFexpress Type A (CEA-G Series)
sdcards.pros: Sony-made, IP57-rated card for the FX3, FX30, A1 and A7R V, including 4K120.
sdcards.cons: Expensive per GB.

sdcards.name: Lexar Professional CFexpress Type A Gold Series
sdcards.pros: Higher-capacity Type A option for Sony FX3 and A1 shooters.
sdcards.cons: Some early batches ran hotter than Sony's own cards during long 4K120 takes.

sdcards.name: ProGrade Digital SDXC UHS-II V90 Cobalt
sdcards.pros: V90 UHS-II card for dual-slot bodies like the Canon R6 Mark II and Fujifilm X-T5.
sdcards.cons: Priced close to the Sony TOUGH G.

sdcards.name: Silicon Power Superior A2 microSDXC
sdcards.pros: Low-cost A2 card for Steam Deck and retro handhelds, up to 1.5TB.
sdcards.cons: Slower sequential speeds than SanDisk and Samsung A2 cards.

sdcards.name: Kioxia Exceria microSD
sdcards.pros: Cheap Class 10 card for firmware updates, retro games and other low-bitrate use.
sdcards.cons: Not V30 rated. No speed headroom for video.

sdcards.name: Samsung EVO Plus microSD
sdcards.pros: V30 and A2 at a low price. A common pick for SD2Vita, where it works up to 512GB.
sdcards.cons: Writes slower than the Samsung PRO Plus.

sdcards.name: Samsung P9 microSD Express
sdcards.pros: Works in Switch 2 for games. Reads up to 800 MB/s.
sdcards.cons: Needs a microSD Express slot for full speed. Costs more per GB than UHS-I.

sdcards.name: SanDisk microSD Express for Nintendo Switch 2
sdcards.pros: Nintendo-licensed card for Switch 2 game storage.
sdcards.cons: Only 256GB. Runs at UHS-I speed in devices without an Express slot.
